name: Donn Ailéin
text: Donn Ailéin heads one of the six Donn entries the Book of Invasions records. The text lists him among the chiefs of the Tuatha Dé Danann. His entry is a brief name record rather than a full tale. MacKillop reads the name as another shape of Donn mac Miled. The name therefore reaches back to Donn the god of the dead. The six-leader frame places Donn Ailéin inside the invasion-list tradition, where several sons of Míl Espáine take the Donn title. The Book of Invasions gives him no separate deeds. Scholars therefore treat him as a doubling of the chief Donn figure rather than an independent person. His listing still documents how widely the name spread through the invasion account.

okr.objective: Record the Donn Ailéin entry of MacKillop's Dictionary of Celtic Mythology as a PCE node grounded in the Lebor Gabála six-Donn listing.
key_results: The node names Donn Ailéin as one of six leaders called Donn in the Book of Invasions.
The node routes him to Donn mac Miled and Donn the god of the dead through the identification MacKillop states.
The node carries the MacKillop 2008 citation and links the named corpus entities.
okr.evidence: MacKillop 2008 article 'Donn Ailéin', Dictionary of Celtic Mythology, s.v. Donn Ailéin.
